clue.text: 26 for setter between future and present

indicators.note: between says the setter's letter sits in the middle, flanked by the future and present tense words

parts.note: will marks the future tense, as in 'I will go'
am is a present-tense form of the verb to be
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: A cryptic remark about a crossword setter caught between tenses.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is the answer to 26-across: this light, like several others, is a variety of that fruit, the Williams or Bartlett pear.
explanation.definitionFit: A Williams is a widely grown variety of pear, so the name stands for an example of the fruit at 26.

clue.text: Court study of Australian 26

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them
a den is a private room for study

explanation.surface: Sounds like a legal study of an Australian matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a law court; it is the verb meaning to pay romantic attention.
explanation.definitionFit: The woody pear (Xylomelum) is an Australian shrub whose hard fruit resembles a pear, hence its common name.

clue.text: A model in 19 should be up to date

indicators.note: in places the article and the model inside the word that answers clue 19

parts.note: the answer to 19-down means 'in case', a sense also carried by lest
T as in the Model T Ford

explanation.surface: Advice that a fashion model should keep current.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 points to the answer of 19-down, whose meaning 'in case' is supplied here by LEST; A plus T goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The most recent thing is fully current, so newest and up to date are synonyms.

clue.text: Hosts of quite good shots — look back inside

indicators.note: inside says the reversed glance is placed within the word for the archery shots

parts.note: in archery and shooting, inners are shots hitting the ring just inside the bull, good but not the best

indicators.note: back says the word for a quick look is turned around

parts.note: to peek is to take a quick look

explanation.surface: A marksman told to look back at their reasonably good shots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite good shots' is archery jargon: an inner is a hit just outside the bull, decent but not top score. 'back' turns the look round before 'inside' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: Landlords of inns host their guests, so innkeepers are hosts in the hospitality sense.

clue.text: Murder's first … victim a girl?

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word murder

parts.note: Abel was the Bible's first murder victim, killed by his brother Cain

explanation.surface: A whodunnit teaser asking whether the victim was a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bible's first murder ties the two parts together neatly: Abel is the archetypal victim.
explanation.definitionFit: Mabel is a female given name, so the answer is an example of a girl.

clue.text: 26 and more than 8 dozen eggs returned at a party

indicators.note: returned means the word for eggs is read backwards

parts.note: ova are eggs in biology
eight dozen is 96, and C, the Roman numeral for 100, is more than that
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone bringing nearly a hundred eggs to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns OVA into AVO. The roundabout 'more than 8 dozen' is the Roman 100, C.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is also called the alligator pear, so it counts as a kind of the fruit at 26.

clue.text: All quiet in a dump — that's all Masefield asked

indicators.note: in places the two words inside the rubbish dump

parts.note: a tip is a rubbish dump in British usage
taken as written
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Masefield's modest wish set against a quiet rubbish dump.
explanation.walkthrough: John Masefield's poem Sea-Fever runs 'And all I ask is a tall ship and a star to steer her by'. TIP is British for a rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: The line from Sea-Fever names the sailing vessel as the poet's whole request, so the quotation defines the phrase.

clue.text: Not being tied, fuel producers rake in one less than 9k

indicators.note: rake in means the oil cartel gathers the shortened nine into its middle

parts.note: OPEC is the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, oil producers

indicators.note: one less than nine here means the number word with its I, the Roman one, taken away

parts.note: the number written as a word
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Oil producers raking in just under nine thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one less than 9' tempts you to 8; here 'one' is the Roman I removed from the spelt-out number, which 'rake in' puts inside the cartel's name before the k.
explanation.definitionFit: A shirt worn with no tie and an unbuttoned collar is said to have this style, so it describes not being tied.

clue.text: Bill's greeting always a success?

parts.note: a bill is an account, abbreviated AC
hi is a greeting
ever means always, as in 'for ever'

explanation.surface: Wondering if a cheerful hello from Bill always succeeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name but is an account (AC).
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is a success has accomplished things, so a person who succeeds is one who accomplishes goals.

clue.text: Feudal superior arriving in Normandy

definitions.meaning: a lord above other lords in the feudal hierarchy
the code name of the Allied D-Day invasion of Normandy in 1944

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a lord with vassal lords under him, and was also the code name for the Normandy landings.

clue.text: Newspaper's one-off round comes many times

indicators.note: round says the scrambled letters surround the newspaper's initials
off says the letters of one are disordered

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper's one-off feature that keeps coming round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one-off' looks like a single event; it splits into the word one and 'off', the anagram signal, and 'round' wraps the result round the paper's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Frequently and many times are synonyms for how regularly something happens.

clue.text: Support film with bird on garden tool with part of car

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
Kes is a 1969 British film about a boy and his kestrel
a hoe is a garden tool

explanation.surface: A jumble of a support, a bird film and a garden tool.
explanation.walkthrough: KES is Ken Loach's film about a Yorkshire boy who trains a kestrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved block pressed against a wheel to slow it is a component of a vehicle's braking system.

clue.text: No problem about turning tiller in white flower

indicators.note: about means the word for no problem goes around the scrambled letters

parts.note: easy means no problem

indicators.note: turning signals that the letters of tiller are rearranged

explanation.surface: Turning a boat's tiller among white flowers is no problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tiller' suggests boats, but it is just anagram fodder for 'turning'; 'about' wraps the phrase for no problem around it.
explanation.definitionFit: This trumpet-shaped white lily is associated with spring religious festivals, a specific white bloom.

clue.text: Man's going to fire

definitions.meaning: he will, contracted with an apostrophe
the fiery place of punishment in the afterlife

explanation.definitionFit: Contracted 'he will' reads the same as the word for the infernal fiery underworld.

clue.text: Communication from party dancing with Hegel

indicators.note: dancing signals that the letters of the two words are moved about

explanation.surface: A party where people dance alongside the philosopher Hegel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges PARTY and HEGEL together.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending messages by wire over distance is a form of communication.

clue.text: Tractarian nobleman without a speed permit

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside: the nobleman goes around the rest

parts.note: a peer is a nobleman
amph is short for amphetamine, slang speed
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A nobleman driving without a speed permit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here. 'Tractarian' usually means an Oxford Movement member, but here it is one who writes tracts.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of tracts, short polemical booklets, can jokingly be called a tractarian.

clue.text: Novel with first part abbreviated: unruly mob around me aren't consistent

indicators.note: around says the scrambled mob encloses the word me
unruly signals that the letters of mob are disordered

parts.note: things that vary are not consistent

explanation.surface: An unruly mob surrounds someone, and things keep changing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' turns MOB into MBO, split around ME to give M-ME-BO. Flaubert's novel Madame Bovary appears with 'Madame' abbreviated as Mme.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaubert's novel Madame Bovary, with its title's first word shortened to Mme, matches the defining phrase.

clue.text: Show disapproval of reactionary legislation by politician to establish reformatory

parts.note: to boo is to show disapproval

indicators.note: reactionary hints at going backwards, so the word for legislation is reversed

parts.note: an act is a piece of legislation
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A political protest at hardline legislation over a reformatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reactionary' reverses ACT to TCA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough training camp for young offenders serves as a corrective institution, a modern reformatory.

clue.text: Height 3π + 50 solved in old battlefield

indicators.note: solved suggests the letters are worked out into a new order

parts.note: three lots of pi, the Greek letter spelled out
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A mathematical equation to be solved.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface looks like algebra; π is just the letters PI, three times over.
explanation.definitionFit: Philippi in Macedonia was the site of the 42 BC battle where Antony and Octavian defeated Brutus and Cassius.

clue.text: Books woman footballer without work for Sartre's 12

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
her refers to a woman

indicators.note: without in the sense of outside: the footballer's name goes around the work

parts.note: Pele was the Brazilian footballer
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Books on a woman footballer with no job.
explanation.walkthrough: In Sartre's play Huis Clos the famous line is 'Hell is other people', and 12-across is HELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Sartre wrote that the infernal torment of 12-across consists of the company of everyone else.

clue.text: Little energy after South Americans packed

indicators.note: after says the energy letter comes behind the South American people

parts.note: the Incas were a South American people
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: South Americans packing despite low energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer means boxed up, or packed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed inside a container has been packed away.

clue.text: Service in the afternoon to tantalise leader of troop

parts.note: to tease is to tantalise

indicators.note: leader of takes just the first letter of troop

explanation.surface: Teasing a troop leader at an afternoon service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like a church service; it is a set of crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: The cups, saucers and pot used for afternoon refreshments make up a crockery service.

clue.text: Ring for 28

definitions.meaning: to sound a bell slowly and repeatedly
a charge paid to use a road or bridge, a kind of payment

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a bell's slow ring and also a fee levied for passage, a form of charge.

clue.text: Powwow for 26

definitions.meaning: a popular British variety of pear

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a formal meeting and is also a common English pear variety.

clue.text: Brilliant clue to the back teeth?

parts.note: brilliant is slang def; in a down entry the letters FED read upwards spell it

explanation.surface: A clever clue that hits you right in the back teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'fed up to the back teeth' gives the definition; the cryptic reading is DEF, slang for brilliant, written up the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Completing the idiom about being thoroughly sick of something, the answer precedes 'to the back teeth'.

clue.text: See 6
Fruit connecting floors

definitions.meaning: Cockney rhyming slang for stairs, which connect floors

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names two orchard fruits and is Cockney rhyming slang for stairs, which link floors.

clue.text: See 25
Thin-skinned 26

definitions.meaning: a cactus fruit known as a type of pear

explanation.definitionFit: The word means touchy or easily offended, and the cactus fruit called the prickly kind is a pear.

clue.text: Charge pet with many mistakes

indicators.note: with many mistakes suggests the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Charging a pet owner for many errors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakes' scrambles PET and MANY together.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is a sum demanded, i.e. money to be paid.
